# OCD & Anxiety Therapy Vancouver & BC | Unravel

Online OCD and anxiety counselling with Theekshitha Vadladi for adults in Vancouver and across BC.

## Care and practical details

Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is the main therapeutic framework. Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) is used for OCD. EMDR is a secondary approach for anxiety and trauma where appropriate. Theekshitha Vadladi is a pre-licensed mental health counsellor with completed training in ACT, ERP for OCD and EMDR basic training with required consultation. Clients must be aged 18+ and physically in BC during sessions. Individual sessions are CAD $145 for 50 minutes or CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. A free 20-minute consultation is available by phone or video.

# OCD Therapy Vancouver & BC | Unravel Counselling

Intrusive thoughts, checking and mental rituals can take up far more of your day than anyone else sees. I offer online OCD counselling for adults, using ERP with support from ACT.

## When the doubt keeps coming back.

You check, feel some relief, then notice another reason to doubt. A conversation gets replayed. A memory needs examining again. You ask someone a question you have already asked, hoping this answer will finally settle it.

OCD counselling looks at this whole sequence: what brings on the doubt, what you do in response, and how that response keeps drawing you back in. The things you want to spend your time doing help us decide where to begin.

## The thought is one part of the picture.

Obsessions are unwanted thoughts, images or urges. Compulsions are actions or mental rituals that a person feels driven to repeat, often to reduce distress or prevent a feared outcome. OCD can attach to many subjects, including harm, relationships, contamination, responsibility or faith.

Some rituals are easy to see. Others happen silently: reviewing a conversation, checking a feeling, repeating a phrase or trying to prove what a thought means. The question is what that response is doing and how much of your life it is taking up.

The [OCD themes guide](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-types/) explains common presentations, including false-memory concerns and what people sometimes call “Pure O”.

## How I work with OCD: ERP and ACT.

I use [Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP)](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/) for the OCD-specific work. We identify situations that bring on obsessions and plan practice responding without the rituals that usually follow. I explain the purpose of a proposed exercise and discuss it with you before we begin.

[Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/) supports this work by helping you respond more flexibly to difficult thoughts and feelings and take part in the things you care about. For OCD, it works alongside ERP.

A useful goal might be finishing a task without prolonged checking, or staying involved in a conversation while doubt is present. We review what changes in daily life, including the less visible rituals that can continue after an exercise.

## Understand what matters before planning a change.

Faith, family and personal responsibilities can be deeply important. They need to be understood when we work out what is a valued practice and what has become a ritual driven by doubt. An unfamiliar belief or cultural practice is not, by itself, a symptom.

As a South Asian woman and first-generation immigrant, I bring that perspective to my work while asking what these experiences mean for you. Adults from all backgrounds are welcome. [Read about me and my completed training.](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)

## How we begin

### A conversation about fit

Use the free 20-minute consultation to ask about OCD counselling, my approach and the practical arrangements.

### Understand your pattern

Early sessions explore the obsessions, visible and mental rituals, daily impact and changes you want help with.

### Plan, practise and review

We agree on a starting point, discuss practice and review what happens. The plan can be adjusted as we learn more.

## Fees and format

Free consultation: 20 minutes, phone or video. Individual session: CAD $145 for 50 minutes. Extended individual session: CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. Adults 18+, virtual, physically located in BC during sessions.

## Common questions

### Do I need an OCD diagnosis before contacting you?

You can enquire without a confirmed diagnosis. Tell me briefly what you are noticing and what you want help with. The consultation is a conversation about fit; it is not a formal diagnostic assessment.

### Can you work with mental compulsions or “Pure O”?

Mental reviewing, checking, neutralising and reassurance seeking can be part of the OCD cycle. We consider their purpose rather than treating every repeated thought as a compulsion. Read the [guide to mental compulsions](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/mental-compulsions-ocd/).

### Are appointments in person or online?

All appointments are online. I work with adults aged 18 and over who are physically in British Columbia during sessions, including Vancouver.

### How many sessions will I need?

The number and frequency depend on the difficulties involved, your goals and how the work is progressing. We discuss this as we go, alongside the time and cost you can commit.

# ERP Therapy for OCD in Vancouver & BC | Unravel

ERP works on the compulsions that keep OCD going, including checking, reassurance seeking and mental rituals. I offer ERP within individual online counselling for adults across BC.

## What is exposure and response prevention?

Exposure means approaching a planned situation, thought, image or other trigger that brings on OCD-related distress. Response prevention means practising without the ritual you would usually use to settle that distress. Both parts matter.

ERP is a form of cognitive behavioural therapy and a first-line psychological treatment for OCD. It combines planned exposure with changing the compulsive response. The [International OCD Foundation explains how ERP works](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/treatment/erp/).

## Planning ERP together.

We begin by understanding the obsessions, compulsions and avoidance affecting you, and what you want to be able to do differently. Practice may involve a real situation or an imagined scenario. We agree on a starting point and discuss what response prevention would involve.

ERP can be challenging. You should understand the purpose of a proposed step and be involved in the decisions; you should not be deceived or forced into an exposure. Genuine health and safety needs, your beliefs and your responsibilities belong in that planning.

The aim is to practise responding differently while uncertainty is present. An exercise cannot prove that a feared event could never happen, and anxiety does not have to disappear during every practice.

## Mental rituals need attention too.

Someone might send an email without rereading it, then spend an hour mentally checking whether it sounded rude. The visible check has stopped, but a less visible ritual may still be continuing.

Mental reviewing, internal reassurance and neutralising can continue after an outward ritual stops. Response prevention looks at the role of that thinking; it does not require a blank mind or treating every unwanted thought as a ritual. [NICE’s OCD recommendations include mental rituals and neutralising strategies](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg31/chapter/Recommendations).

[Read about mental compulsions](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/mental-compulsions-ocd/) and [rumination in OCD](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/rumination-ocd/).

## Practice and review between sessions.

Sessions take place online, with practice during and between appointments where appropriate. We discuss what you will try, how it fits into your week and what to notice. At the next appointment, we look at what happened and what got in the way.

We review changes in time spent on rituals, avoidance and participation in daily life. An exercise can still teach us something when it feels difficult. If it is not helping, we revisit the plan, including whether mental rituals are continuing.

## How ACT supports ERP.

[ACT](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/) can help you make space for discomfort while choosing an action connected to your values. In OCD care, this supports ERP and keeps the practice connected to the parts of life you want to return to.

I have completed a four-day ERP intensive through Cognitive Behavior Institute with Alissa Jerud, PhD. [View the full training details.](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/#training)

## How we begin

### Map what happens

Identify triggers, compulsions, avoidance and the effect on your day.

### Choose a starting point

Discuss a specific practice, its purpose and the response you will work on.

### Learn from the practice

Review visible and mental responses, obstacles and progress towards your goals.

## Fees and format

Free consultation: 20 minutes, phone or video. Individual session: CAD $145 for 50 minutes. Extended individual session: CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. Adults 18+, virtual, physically located in BC during sessions.

## Common questions

### Can ERP therapy be done online?

Yes. Sessions at Unravel are online for adults physically located in BC. We plan practice that suits the online setting and discuss a private place to meet.

### Will I have to start with my biggest fear?

We discuss practice opportunities and agree on a starting point. You should understand what is proposed and have a say in the plan. ERP can feel challenging; it should not involve surprise or forced exposures.

### Is ERP a type of CBT?

Yes. ERP is a specific form of cognitive behavioural therapy developed to address obsessions and compulsions.

### What happens in the first ERP session?

We begin with how OCD affects your day, what you do in response to distress, and what you want help with. I explain how ERP could fit and discuss a possible starting point. The [what-to-expect page](https://unravelcounselling.com/about/) explains the first appointments.

### What does ERP therapy cost?

The individual counselling rates apply: CAD $145 for 50 minutes or CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places may be available. [See fees and session options.](https://unravelcounselling.com/low-cost-counselling-bc/)

# Anxiety Counselling Vancouver & BC | Unravel Counselling

When worry follows you through work, decisions and time with other people, counselling can help you understand what is happening and practise a different response. I work online with adults across BC, using ACT.

## When worry starts making your decisions.

You might spend the evening preparing for problems that have not happened, put off a decision until you feel more certain, or leave a conversation wondering how you came across. Even rest can turn into another thing to get right.

In anxiety therapy, we look at the worry, tension and avoidance affecting you, as well as the pressures you are actually living with. Your goals help us decide which part of that picture to work on first.

## What ACT-based anxiety counselling involves.

[Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/) is the main approach in my work. It helps you notice thoughts and feelings, respond with more flexibility and take steps towards the things you care about.

We might work through a recent situation where anxiety changed what you did. What showed up? How did you respond? What happened afterwards? I may suggest a short exercise or a different response to practise, and explain what we are trying to learn.

A goal might be contributing to a meeting, making a decision with some uncertainty, or spending time with a friend without closely monitoring yourself. The step we choose needs to make sense in your life.

## Work, family and the pressures around you.

Workload, finances, discrimination, migration and family expectations can place real demands on you. We consider those circumstances alongside your responses to worry. Practical changes and sources of support can be part of the conversation.

I ask what culture, faith and relationships mean to you, and which responsibilities you want to honour. [Read about me and my approach.](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)

## When worry and OCD overlap.

Repeated checking, reassurance seeking or mental reviewing may need a closer look at an OCD-related cycle. [OCD counselling at Unravel](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/) includes ERP for that work. You can enquire without having decided which label fits.

Where distressing experiences are relevant, [EMDR](https://unravelcounselling.com/emdr-therapy-bc/) may be considered as a secondary approach. We discuss the reasons for any approach I suggest and whether the service fits what you need.

## How we begin

### Talk about what you need

The free consultation covers what you are looking for, my approach and practical questions.

### Understand the difficulty

Early sessions explore how worry and avoidance affect your day, what you have tried and what you want to change.

### Practise and check in

We agree on useful steps and review what is changing between appointments. Your feedback is part of that review.

## Fees and format

Free consultation: 20 minutes, phone or video. Individual session: CAD $145 for 50 minutes. Extended individual session: CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. Adults 18+, virtual, physically located in BC during sessions.

## Common questions

### Can I enquire without an anxiety diagnosis?

Yes. Describe what you are finding difficult and the support you are looking for. You do not need to arrive with a diagnosis or a complete explanation.

### Do you offer online anxiety therapy outside Vancouver?

Yes. I work online with adults aged 18 and over across British Columbia. You need to be physically located in BC during each session.

### How is ACT different from trying to think positively?

ACT works on how you relate to thoughts and feelings and how you choose your next action. It does not depend on replacing every anxious thought with a positive one.

### How often would we meet?

We discuss frequency in relation to your goals, the work involved, your availability and budget. We review the plan as counselling continues.

### What if counselling is not helping?

Please tell me. We can revisit our understanding of the difficulty, the goals or the way we are working. The [what-to-expect page](https://unravelcounselling.com/about/#reviewing) explains how feedback and adjustments fit into care.

## Where to next

- [How ACT is used](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/)
- [OCD and compulsive responses](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/)
- [EMDR for anxiety and trauma](https://unravelcounselling.com/emdr-therapy-bc/)
- [Fees and reduced-fee availability](https://unravelcounselling.com/low-cost-counselling-bc/)
- [OCD versus anxiety](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/ocd-vs-anxiety/)

# ACT Therapy Vancouver & BC | Unravel Counselling

Acceptance and Commitment Therapy helps you respond to difficult thoughts and feelings while making choices connected to what matters to you. ACT is the main approach in my online counselling work with adults across BC.

## What is Acceptance and Commitment Therapy?

ACT, pronounced as the word “act”, is a behavioural therapy focused on psychological flexibility. That means noticing what is happening, making room for internal experiences and choosing a response that serves your life.

A thought can feel convincing and still leave you with a choice about what to do next. In therapy, we explore that choice through the situations you want help with.

## Start with something that happened in your week.

We might take an avoided decision, a familiar worry or a conversation that was difficult. I ask what thoughts and feelings showed up, what you did and how that affected the things you wanted to do.

I may suggest a brief exercise to help you notice a thought, redirect attention or try a different response. I explain its purpose and ask what you notice. The language, example and pace can be adjusted when they do not fit.

Between appointments, we may agree on a small action connected to your goals. The next session gives us a chance to review what happened and what you learned.

## Whose idea of a meaningful life?

Values describe qualities you want to bring to how you live: perhaps care, honesty, learning or connection. I ask what those ideas mean to you rather than assuming we share a definition.

Culture, faith, family and responsibilities belong in that discussion. You may want to honour a commitment while changing how you respond to an expectation. Acceptance in ACT concerns internal experiences; it does not require accepting a harmful situation.

## ACT for OCD: supporting ERP.

For OCD, I use ACT alongside [Exposure and Response Prevention](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/). ERP works on the compulsive response. ACT helps you make space for discomfort and connect that practice with the life OCD has been interrupting.

For example, attending a family meal might matter more to you than finishing the evening with complete certainty about a thought. That personal reason can guide practice and help you keep taking part while uncertainty remains.

## Six connected ways of building flexibility.

ACT brings together six processes. They are ways of working, rather than a checklist you have to complete.

- Acceptance: making room for feelings that arise while doing something meaningful.
- Defusion: noticing a thought without automatically treating it as an instruction.
- Present-moment awareness: bringing attention back to what is happening now.
- Perspective: recognising that a thought or feeling is part of your experience, rather than the whole of who you are.
- Values: clarifying the qualities you want to express in how you live.
- Committed action: taking steps in those directions and adjusting as you learn.

## How we begin

### Choose a direction

Talk about the parts of life you want help with and the changes that would matter to you.

### Understand your responses

Explore how thoughts, feelings and familiar actions affect those possibilities.

### Try something and review it

Practise a response or action, then use your experience to decide what needs attention next.

## Fees and format

Free consultation: 20 minutes, phone or video. Individual session: CAD $145 for 50 minutes. Extended individual session: CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. Adults 18+, virtual, physically located in BC during sessions.

## Common questions

### How is ACT used for anxiety?

We look at how worry and avoidance affect your choices and practise responding in ways that support your goals. [Read about anxiety counselling.](https://unravelcounselling.com/anxiety-counselling-bc/)

### Does acceptance mean agreeing with a thought?

No. You can notice a thought or feeling without believing it, acting on it or approving of it.

### Do I need to meditate?

No previous meditation experience is needed. Exercises are introduced in ordinary language and connected to the work you are doing.

### Will ACT stop anxious thoughts?

The focus is on how you respond to thoughts and feelings and how you participate in your life. We review progress in relation to your goals, rather than promising that difficult thoughts will disappear.

# EMDR Therapy Vancouver & BC | Unravel Counselling

EMDR may be considered when distressing experiences remain connected to the difficulties you are having now. I offer it as a secondary approach within online counselling for adults across BC.

## What is EMDR therapy?

Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing is a structured psychotherapy used in trauma treatment. It includes understanding your history, preparation, memory processing, session closure and review. Bilateral stimulation, such as guided eye movements, is one part of that wider process.

Clinical guidelines support EMDR for PTSD and clinically important PTSD symptoms. [NICE describes a phased approach delivered by trained practitioners](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng116/chapter/Recommendations). At Unravel, I consider EMDR for anxiety and trauma where appropriate; the reason for suggesting it needs to be clear in relation to your difficulties.

## Begin with understanding and preparation.

Early appointments focus on what brings you to counselling, relevant experiences, current difficulties and goals. Preparation includes discussing how the approach works, ways to manage distress, and the practical arrangements for meeting online.

You can ask about the purpose of each part of the work and discuss readiness, pacing and pauses. Preparation may take more than one appointment. We also consider how to close a session and review what happens afterwards.

## When I may suggest EMDR.

[ACT](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/) is the main framework in my practice. EMDR may be considered where distressing experiences are relevant to anxiety or trauma-related difficulties. I explain why I am suggesting an approach and discuss it with you.

If [OCD](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/) and compulsions are central to the difficulty, [ERP](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/) provides the OCD-specific work. We choose the approach in relation to the pattern we are working on.

## Plan for privacy and a suitable place to meet.

All appointments take place online. We discuss a private space, a reliable connection, possible interruptions and what to do if the connection drops. Those arrangements are part of deciding whether the online setting is suitable for the proposed work.

I have completed both parts of EMDR basic training and the required consultation through EMDR Training Associates. [Read the full training details.](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/#training)

## How we begin

### Discuss what you need

Use the free consultation to ask about the approach, online format and fit.

### Understand and prepare

Early sessions explore your experiences, goals and preparation for the proposed work.

### Work at an agreed pace

Review how the work is affecting you and discuss adjustments or other care where needed.

## Fees and format

Free consultation: 20 minutes, phone or video. Individual session: CAD $145 for 50 minutes. Extended individual session: CAD $190 for 90 minutes. Limited reduced-fee places depend on availability. Adults 18+, virtual, physically located in BC during sessions.

## Common questions

### Can EMDR be offered online?

EMDR can be provided online when it is clinically appropriate and the setting is suitable. We discuss the practical arrangements and whether that format fits your circumstances.

### Will we process memories in the first appointment?

The first appointments focus on understanding your needs and preparing for the work. There is no fixed timetable for beginning memory processing.

### Is EMDR the main treatment for OCD at Unravel?

No. ERP provides the OCD-specific work on compulsions. ACT supports that work. EMDR is a secondary approach considered for anxiety and trauma where appropriate.

### How much does EMDR therapy cost?

The individual counselling rates apply: CAD $145 for 50 minutes or CAD $190 for 90 minutes. We discuss the appropriate session option in relation to the work. Limited reduced-fee places may be available. [See fees and insurance information.](https://unravelcounselling.com/low-cost-counselling-bc/)

### Who can book?

I work with adults aged 18 and over who are physically in British Columbia during appointments. You can begin with a free 20-minute phone or video consultation.

The individual rates apply to OCD and anxiety counselling, including ACT, ERP or EMDR where appropriate. Reduced-fee places are limited and can be discussed during the consultation if available; no reduced rate is guaranteed in advance. Sessions are virtual for adults aged 18+ physically in BC.

Theekshitha Vadladi is a pre-licensed mental health counsellor offering individual online OCD and anxiety counselling to adults in British Columbia.

## Care and practical details

Theekshitha has completed all requirements for the Master of Arts (MA) in Counselling Psychology at Adler University; degree conferral is pending. Theekshitha holds a BA in Psychology from the University of British Columbia and practises as a pre-licensed mental health counsellor. Her approach uses ACT, with ERP for OCD and EMDR for anxiety and trauma where appropriate, with attention to culture and the person’s circumstances. # About Unravel Counselling

How counselling begins at Unravel: the free 20-minute consultation, first paid appointments, individual planning and review.

## Care and practical details

We’ll use this phone or video call to talk about what you want help with and whether my practice is a good fit. I’ll ask for a brief sense of what has been happening, what you’re hoping counselling could change, and any previous therapy you want me to know about. I’ll explain how I might work with you, answer your questions, and go over fees and appointment options. You can take time afterwards to decide whether you’d like to book a session. We’ll begin with the difficulties that brought you here and how they are affecting your day. I’ll ask about what you’ve tried, what has helped, and what you would like to be able to do more freely. We’ll also talk through confidentiality and the arrangements for working together online. If OCD is part of what you’re experiencing, I’ll ask about checking, reassurance, avoidance and the rituals that can happen entirely in your head. This helps us understand what happens around a distressing thought and where counselling could help. We may need more than one appointment to build that picture. I’ll explain my initial understanding and discuss a starting point with you. Your goals give the work a direction. That might mean getting through a morning without repeated checking, spending less time caught in worry, or returning to something you’ve been avoiding. In anxiety counselling, we’ll use ACT to work on how you respond to worry and avoidance, with steps connected to what you want to do. For OCD, we’ll plan ERP around the situations and compulsions affecting you. ACT can help connect that practice with the life you want to take part in. We’ll discuss what an exercise involves, why I’m suggesting it, and how it fits your circumstances. Culture and faith can change what needs to be understood before choosing a step. For someone whose faith matters deeply, that can include distinguishing a valued religious practice from a ritual driven by doubt. We’ll also consider privacy, responsibilities and the time available for practice. I’ll ask how the sessions are landing and what is changing outside them. You can tell me when an explanation misses the point, an exercise feels confusing, or we’re spending time on something that matters less to you. We’ll look at what needs adjusting: our understanding of the difficulty, the goals, the practice or the way I’m explaining it. In OCD work, that includes noticing whether a visible ritual has been replaced by mental checking. Progress might show up as less time spent on rituals or more participation in daily life, even while some anxiety remains. If your needs would be better met by a different clinician or service, I’ll discuss that with you and help you consider the options.

## Where to next

- [OCD therapy](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/)

# Types of OCD: Common Themes & Examples | Unravel

A guide to common OCD themes and the visible and mental compulsions that may accompany them.

## Care and practical details

Themes describe the subject of an OCD concern, rather than a separate diagnosis for every topic. Themes can overlap or change. This guide covers contamination, just-right feelings, checking and responsibility, harm-related thoughts, relationship-focused doubt, scrupulosity, and memory-related doubt. It explains mental reviewing and the phrase pure O. A single unwanted thought or matching description does not establish OCD. ERP addresses compulsive responses; ACT supports values and psychological flexibility. Individual virtual counselling is available to adults aged 18+ physically in BC, including Vancouver.

## Where to next

- [Online OCD therapy](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/)
- [Exposure and Response Prevention](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/)
- [ACT in OCD care](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/)
- [OCD and anxiety resources](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/)

# Mental Compulsions in OCD: The Rituals You Cannot See

Someone can look still while spending hours reviewing, checking or trying to undo a thought. Understanding the purpose of that thinking helps explain mental compulsions.

By [Theekshitha Vadladi](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)

Published: 2026-11-03

General information to support a conversation about care. This article does not diagnose your experience or provide an individual treatment plan.

## What is a mental compulsion?

A mental compulsion is a repeated internal act performed in response to an obsession or a rule someone feels driven to follow. It may aim to reduce distress, prevent a feared outcome or reach a feeling of certainty. The ritual happens in thought, so it can be difficult for other people to notice.

In OCD, a person may repeatedly reconstruct a conversation, count silently, replace an unwanted thought with another thought, or check whether a feeling is present. What matters is the role the response plays in the pattern. Remembering an event or repeating a phrase is not automatically a compulsion.

Sources: [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/); [NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over).

## Examples of rituals that happen internally

Consider someone who remembers a conversation and worries that a comment revealed something terrible about them. They replay the wording, inspect their intentions and search their memory for a detail that would settle the concern. An answer briefly feels convincing, until another possible interpretation appears.

That example illustrates a possible OCD cycle, rather than a way to identify OCD from one situation. Internal responses can take different forms, including:

- Mental reviewing: replaying events or conversations to resolve doubt.
- Neutralising: using a thought, image or phrase to try to cancel another one.
- Internal checking: repeatedly inspecting feelings, intentions or bodily reactions.
- Counting or repeating: following an internal sequence until a rule or feeling of completeness is met.

Sources: [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/); [IOCDF: Understanding compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/).

## Why the answer may never feel finished

A ritual may bring short-lived relief. The problem is that the next doubt can call for another round, and the demand for certainty grows harder to satisfy. Time and attention become organised around answering the concern instead of taking part in the day.

This helps explain why more reasoning does not always feel useful. The issue may be the repeated attempt to obtain certainty, rather than a missing piece of information. Compulsive reviewing can also occur after a visible ritual or an exposure, so the full sequence deserves attention.

Sources: [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/); [IOCDF: Understanding compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/).

- [Read about rumination in OCD](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/rumination-ocd/)

## Ordinary reflection and valued practices need context

People think carefully about mistakes, reflect on relationships and use repeated words in meaningful ways. Prayer, for example, can be an important religious practice. Its form alone cannot tell us whether a compulsive process is involved.

A useful clinical conversation considers the purpose, rigidity, distress and effect on life. Faith and cultural commitments deserve respectful understanding. It also matters whether trying to classify every thought as a ritual has itself become another time-consuming search for certainty.

Sources: [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/); [IOCDF: OCD and scrupulosity](https://iocdf.org/faith-ocd/what-is-ocd-scrupulosity/).

- [Explore common OCD themes](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-types/)

## How ERP includes mental rituals

Exposure and Response Prevention is a form of cognitive behavioural therapy used for OCD. Exposure involves planned contact with a trigger; response prevention addresses the ritual that usually follows. When the ritual is mental, that internal response belongs in the plan.

Response prevention does not require an empty mind. A thought appearing and the effort to neutralise or repeatedly resolve it are different parts of the experience. Understanding that distinction helps identify what is being practised. The starting point and pace need to be planned for the individual.

At Unravel, ACT is the main framework and ERP is used for OCD. ACT supports willingness, attention and action guided by values alongside the OCD-specific work. The purpose is connected with the life the rituals are interrupting.

Sources: [IOCDF: Exposure and Response Prevention](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/); [ACBS: The six core processes of ACT](https://contextualscience.org/six_core_processes_act).

- [How ERP works](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/)
- [ACT at Unravel](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/)

## What to bring to a first conversation

A broad description is enough to begin: what tends to trigger the loop, what you feel driven to do mentally and how much it interrupts your day. Questions about training, mental rituals and the proposed approach can help you consider whether a service is appropriate.

Unravel offers virtual individual OCD counselling for adults aged 18 and over who are physically in British Columbia, including Vancouver. A free 20-minute phone or video consultation covers the approach, fees and availability.

- [Explore online OCD counselling](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/)
- [Meet Theekshitha Vadladi](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)

- [Meet the author](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)

- [IOCDF: Understanding compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/)
- [NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over)

- [IOCDF: Exposure and Response Prevention](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/)
- [ACBS: The six core processes of ACT](https://contextualscience.org/six_core_processes_act)

# Rumination and OCD: When Thinking Becomes a Ritual

One more replay, one more explanation, one more attempt to be sure. Rumination can feel like problem-solving while keeping the original doubt open.

By [Theekshitha Vadladi](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)

Published: 2026-11-03

General information to support a conversation about care. This article does not diagnose your experience or provide an individual treatment plan.

## Can rumination be an OCD compulsion?

Yes. Repeated reasoning or mental reviewing can function as a compulsion when it is used to resolve an obsessional doubt. The thinking may concern a past event, a relationship, morality or another subject that feels urgent to settle.

Rumination also occurs outside OCD. Its presence does not establish a diagnosis. To understand it, a clinical conversation looks at what sets it off, the response it calls for and the effect on a person’s life, rather than relying on the topic alone.

Sources: [IOCDF: Compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/); [Ghaznavi, Schiewe and Stern: Management of rumination and obsessions in primary care](https://www.psychiatrist.com/pcc/management-rumination-obsessions-primary-care/).

## The answer that keeps needing another answer

Imagine reviewing an email because you worry that it sounded unkind. You reconstruct why you chose each word, compare possible interpretations and consider what the recipient might think. For a moment, one explanation seems sufficient. Then a different possibility pulls you back into the review.

The difficulty is not necessarily a lack of effort. The person may be working intensely to solve the concern. But a process organised around complete certainty can keep reopening a question whenever another possibility appears. Meanwhile, rest, work or a conversation happening in the present becomes harder to return to.

Sources: [IOCDF: Compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/).

## Reflection usually has a practical purpose

Looking back on an experience can help someone understand what happened, decide whether an action is needed or learn for next time. Compulsive reviewing may keep searching after the available information has already been considered, because the stopping point depends on feeling certain.

This is a distinction to explore with care, not a rule for policing every thought. A rigid effort to decide whether each moment of thinking is healthy reflection or rumination can itself become another loop. Context, function and the wider pattern matter.

The question is also broader than whether the event was real. OCD-related doubt can concern an actual experience, an imagined possibility or uncertainty about memory. A label such as real-event or false-memory OCD does not establish what happened.

Sources: [IOCDF: Compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/); [Ghaznavi, Schiewe and Stern: Management of rumination and obsessions in primary care](https://www.psychiatrist.com/pcc/management-rumination-obsessions-primary-care/).

- [OCD themes and memory-related doubt](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-types/)

## Why reassurance may become part of the loop

Reviewing sometimes moves between internal analysis and asking another person to confirm an interpretation. Searching online can serve a similar purpose. A reply may settle one version of the concern while leaving room for another question.

The relevant issue is how the response functions. Asking for information or support is part of ordinary life; repeated attempts to obtain certainty may be relevant to an OCD care plan. The full sequence can include less visible responses that happen after the conversation ends.

Sources: [IOCDF: Compulsive reasoning and mental reviewing](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/how-do-i-stop-thinking-about-this-what-to-do-when-youre-stuck-playing-mental-ping-pong/).

- [Mental compulsions explained](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/mental-compulsions-ocd/)
- [Read about reassurance seeking in OCD](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/reassurance-seeking-ocd/)

## How ERP and ACT approach the pattern

ERP combines planned contact with OCD triggers and practice changing compulsive responses. If repeated mental review follows a trigger, response prevention needs to account for it. The work is more specific than trying to think positively or distracting yourself until the question goes away.

At Unravel, ACT provides the main therapeutic framework, with ERP for OCD. ACT brings attention to psychological flexibility and chosen values. A goal might involve being more present with a friend or completing a task without giving the rest of the evening to review.

Practice is selected collaboratively and reviewed in relation to the individual pattern. An educational article cannot determine the right starting point, the relevant mental ritual or the pace for someone it has never met.

Sources: [IOCDF: Exposure and Response Prevention](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/); [ACBS: The six core processes of ACT](https://contextualscience.org/six_core_processes_act).

- [Exposure and Response Prevention](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/)
- [Acceptance and Commitment Therapy](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/)

## Asking for help while the doubt is unfinished

A first conversation can begin with the loop and its cost. It does not require a final answer to the original question. Ask how the counsellor identifies mental rituals, plans response prevention and reviews the effect on daily life.

Unravel offers online OCD and anxiety counselling for adults physically located in BC, including Vancouver. A free 20-minute phone or video consultation is available for questions about the approach, fees and current availability.

- [OCD counselling at Unravel](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/)
- [Consultation details](https://unravelcounselling.com/contact/)

- [Ghaznavi, Schiewe and Stern: Management of rumination and obsessions in primary care](https://www.psychiatrist.com/pcc/management-rumination-obsessions-primary-care/)

# OCD vs Anxiety: Why the Pattern Matters

Anxiety can occur within OCD and alongside it. Looking at what happens after a thought appears helps explain why the distinction matters for treatment.

By [Theekshitha Vadladi](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)

Published: 2026-11-03

General information to support a conversation about care. This article does not diagnose your experience or provide an individual treatment plan.

## What is the difference between OCD and anxiety?

Anxiety is a feeling that can occur in ordinary life and in several mental health conditions. OCD is characterised by obsessions, compulsions or both, with significant distress or interference. Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) involves persistent, difficult-to-control worry across areas of life.

These descriptions overlap in experience. A person can feel anxious because of an OCD obsession, and OCD can occur alongside an anxiety disorder. “OCD or anxiety?” is therefore not always an either-or question.

Sources: [NIMH: Generalized anxiety disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/generalized-anxiety-disorder-gad); [NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over).

## In OCD, the response to doubt needs attention

Obsessions can be unwanted thoughts, images or urges. Compulsions are repetitive behaviours or mental acts that someone feels driven to carry out, often to reduce distress or prevent a feared outcome. Checking, washing, repeated reassurance-seeking and mental reviewing can be part of the pattern.

A person may appear calm while performing internal rituals. The relevant questions include what triggers the response, what it is intended to achieve and how it affects daily life. Having an upsetting thought or preferring order does not, by itself, establish OCD.

Sources: [NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over); [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/).

- [Mental compulsions in OCD](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/mental-compulsions-ocd/)
- [OCD counselling](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/)

## Persistent worry can spread across daily life

In GAD, worry may concern work, health, finances, family or several areas at once. Feeling on edge, tension, poor sleep and difficulty concentrating may accompany it. Duration, frequency, impact and the wider health picture matter to assessment.

Anxiety counselling can begin with the experience rather than a label: the decisions you avoid, the preparation that never feels sufficient, or the effort it takes to get through the day. Real pressures such as financial strain and discrimination belong in that understanding too.

Sources: [NIMH: Generalized anxiety disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/generalized-anxiety-disorder-gad).

- [Anxiety counselling at Unravel](https://unravelcounselling.com/anxiety-counselling-bc/)

## Realistic concerns and intrusive thoughts can overlap

The subject of a thought does not reliably settle the distinction. Health, family and responsibility can appear in ordinary worry, OCD and other difficulties. A thought about a real concern does not automatically rule OCD out, and an unusual thought does not automatically establish it.

For example, reviewing an email might support a practical correction in one situation. In another, it might become a repeated attempt to settle an obsessional doubt. The action can look similar while its function and place in the wider pattern differ.

This is why symptom comparisons can only go so far. If repeated searches for the right diagnosis have themselves become time-consuming, that experience is relevant to bring into a clinical conversation.

Sources: [NIMH: Generalized anxiety disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/generalized-anxiety-disorder-gad); [NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over); [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/).

## Why the distinction changes the treatment discussion

ERP is a first-line psychological treatment for OCD. It combines planned contact with triggers and practice changing compulsive responses, including mental rituals. A plan that overlooks the rituals may miss an important part of the difficulty.

At Unravel, ACT is the main framework for counselling, with ERP used for OCD. ACT supports awareness, psychological flexibility and actions guided by values. In anxiety care, the work considers responses to worry and avoidance in relation to the person’s needs and circumstances.

The role of a method should be clear. Asking how a proposed approach addresses your particular pattern is more useful than selecting a therapy solely because its name is familiar.

Sources: [IOCDF: Exposure and Response Prevention](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/); [ACBS: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy](https://contextualscience.org/act).

- [ERP for OCD](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/)
- [ACT and psychological flexibility](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/)

## Where to begin if you are unsure

Describe what happens, what you feel driven to do next and what the pattern interrupts. Ask about the practice’s scope, the counsellor’s training and whether another assessment would be useful. If you need a formal diagnosis or report, raise that need when enquiring.

Unravel offers virtual individual counselling for adults aged 18 and over who are physically located in British Columbia, including Vancouver. The free 20-minute phone or video consultation covers fit and practical questions; it is not a formal diagnostic assessment.

- [Education and training](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)
- [Fees and consultation options](https://unravelcounselling.com/low-cost-counselling-bc/)

## Where to next

- [Blog and resources](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/)
- [Meet the author](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)
- [NIMH: Generalized anxiety disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/generalized-anxiety-disorder-gad)
- [NIMH: Obsessive-compulsive disorder](https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/publications/obsessive-compulsive-disorder-when-unwanted-thoughts-or-repetitive-behaviors-take-over)
- [International OCD Foundation: What is OCD?](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/)
- [IOCDF: Exposure and Response Prevention](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/)
- [ACBS: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy](https://contextualscience.org/act)

# Reassurance Seeking in OCD: Why the Same Question Keeps Coming Back

You send a quick text, then wonder if it came across as rude. You ask your partner to read it. Their answer helps, until you remember how long your friend took to reply. By bedtime, you want your partner to read the whole thread.

By [Theekshitha Vadladi](https://unravelcounselling.com/counsellor/)

Published: 2026-11-16

General information to support a conversation about care. This article does not diagnose your experience or provide an individual treatment plan.

## What is reassurance seeking in OCD?

In OCD, reassurance seeking can function as a compulsion when getting an answer becomes a way to relieve distress or feel certain about a fear. In the text-message example, you already have your partner’s reading of the message. The next question tries to settle something the first answer couldn’t guarantee: how your friend took it.

Relief can make asking again feel like the next logical step. It can also leave the person answering feeling responsible for finding the exact words that will finally settle the worry.

Sources: [Halldorsson and Salkovskis: Why do people with OCD and health anxiety seek reassurance excessively?](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5504131/); [Salkovskis and Kobori: Self-reported patterns of responses to reassurance seeking in OCD](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26433701/).

## What does reassurance seeking look like?

The same urge can show up as a question to someone else, another online search or a search through your own memory.

- After a small mistake at work has been corrected, asking several colleagues to confirm that nobody was harmed by it.
- Entering the same worry into a search engine or AI chat in different words after the first answer brought brief relief.
- Replaying a conversation or silently listing evidence until you feel certain about what you meant.

Sources: [Halldorsson and Salkovskis: Why do people with OCD and health anxiety seek reassurance excessively?](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5504131/); [Salkovskis and Kobori: Self-reported patterns of responses to reassurance seeking in OCD](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26433701/); [International OCD Foundation: Digital reassurance seeking in OCD](https://iocdf.org/blog/2026/07/21/digital-reassurance-seeking-in-ocd/).

- [How mental reviewing can become a compulsion](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/rumination-ocd/)

## How is reassurance different from asking for help?

Asking someone to clarify a confusing message can give you new information. Calling a friend when you feel overwhelmed can give you company. In a reassurance loop, an answer can feel inadequate even when it addresses the question, because you’re hoping it will settle the fear completely.

The purpose and context of the question matter. New information, a safety concern or a relationship problem can call for a practical response. If you’re unsure what’s driving the pattern, a counsellor can help you look at when it happens, what you do with the answers and how much of your day it takes up.

Sources: [Halldorsson and Salkovskis: Why do people with OCD and health anxiety seek reassurance excessively?](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5504131/); [The Cognitive Behaviour Therapist: Supporting people with OCD and loved ones to move from safety seeking to support](https://doi.org/10.1017/S1754470X22000186).

- [OCD and anxiety can overlap](https://unravelcounselling.com/blog/ocd-vs-anxiety/)

## When you feel the urge to ask again

If you’re trying to understand your pattern, one recent example is enough to bring to counselling. What did you want the answer to settle? When the relief faded, where did you look next?

You might stop asking your partner about the message and still find yourself scanning their expression, rereading the chat or opening a search tab. Mention those quieter responses too. They help a counsellor see where the search for certainty continues and plan practice around the ways it actually shows up for you.

Sources: [Salkovskis and Kobori: Self-reported patterns of responses to reassurance seeking in OCD](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26433701/); [International OCD Foundation: Digital reassurance seeking in OCD](https://iocdf.org/blog/2026/07/21/digital-reassurance-seeking-in-ocd/); [International OCD Foundation: Exposure and Response Prevention](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/).

## What can loved ones say when the question keeps coming back?

It makes sense to want to ease someone’s distress. Talk at a calmer time about what kind of support would feel helpful when the question returns. If you’ve agreed how to handle that moment, you might say, “I can see this is hard. Want me to sit with you for a bit?”

Quiet company might feel right for one person. Someone else might want you to carry on making dinner with them. If answering has become part of your routine together, a counsellor can help you agree on a gradual change that fits your relationship, family roles or cultural expectations.

Sources: [The Cognitive Behaviour Therapist: Supporting people with OCD and loved ones to move from safety seeking to support](https://doi.org/10.1017/S1754470X22000186); [NICE: OCD treatment recommendations, including family involvement and reassurance seeking](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg31/chapter/Recommendations).

## How does ERP address reassurance seeking?

Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) is a first-line psychological treatment for OCD. Exposure involves approaching a situation or doubt that brings up distress. Response prevention involves practising a different response to the urge to do the ritual. You and your counsellor decide together what to practise and at what pace.

Take the text-message example. The uncertainty might be, “My friend may have read my message as rude.” In a low-stakes situation chosen together, the person and counsellor might agree to leave the message as sent and practise going through dinner without asking their partner to interpret it again. Afterward, they could review when the urge was strongest, whether rereading took over and what helped the person stay present at dinner while the question still felt open.

At Unravel, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) supports ERP work by helping you make room for discomfort and keep taking part in what matters to you.

Sources: [NICE: OCD treatment recommendations, including family involvement and reassurance seeking](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg31/chapter/Recommendations); [International OCD Foundation: Exposure and Response Prevention](https://iocdf.org/about-ocd/ocd-treatment-guide/erp/).

- [What ERP involves](https://unravelcounselling.com/erp-therapy-bc/)
- [How Unravel uses ACT](https://unravelcounselling.com/act-therapy-bc/)

## Getting help for OCD reassurance seeking in Vancouver and BC

OCD and anxiety are the focus of Unravel Counselling. Theekshitha Vadladi offers individual online OCD counselling for adults aged 18 and over who are physically in British Columbia, including Vancouver. The work can address reassurance-seeking alongside checking, avoidance and mental rituals.

If the same questions are taking up more of your day, you can bring one ordinary example to a free 20-minute consultation: what set off the doubt, where you looked for an answer and what the search interrupted. You can ask how ERP would fit your situation, how online sessions work and what they cost.

- [Explore online OCD counselling](https://unravelcounselling.com/ocd-therapy-vancouver/)
